source_user: A sparse MoE service has uneven expert load and tail latency. Analyze likely causes and experiments. Scenario variant 114: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure routing distribution, expert capacity overflow, all-to-all time, token dropping/padding, placement, batch composition, and compare routing/capacity policies.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: the checkpoint, expert count, top-k, precision, kernels, runtime, hardware/topology, placement, autoscaling, offered load, concurrency, and request-length mix are fixed; report measured milliseconds, token counts, rates, and confidence intervals, and label estimates. Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 114: routing skew or capacity pressure is the primary cause of the p99 tail; at unchanged offered load, a preregistered treatment of routing/load balancing will lower maximum per-expert load, overflow/drop/padding, and p99 without degrading held-out quality, goodput, SLO attainment, or exceeding the cost budget. Run matched replicas with fixed-seed randomized requests, one policy change at a time, tuning only on a disjoint set, then evaluate a held-out replay and unchanged-load canary. Instrument router scores/entropy and assignment distribution; per-expert tokens, capacity, overflow, drops, padding, utilization; queue, expert compute, dispatch/combine, all-to-all/link time; placement/topology; batch and sequence composition; throughput, p50/p95/p99, quality, goodput, SLOs, errors, retries, memory, and cost. Stratify by expert, sequence length, tenant, concurrency, and load. Control for queueing, warm-up, batching, input mix, autoscaling, network contention, kernel/compiler changes, and correlated retries; randomize paired trials and use bootstrap intervals. Declare success only if tail and load metrics improve with non-inferior quality and no safety/SLO regression. Roll back on error/quality/SLO/cost thresholds or unstable overflow. Do not infer causality from correlation; collect domain-expert review before production use.
